content: {"summary":"To distinguish CPX‑W430 caused by a rolling restart from CPX‑W430 caused by a missing proxy instance, check the rollout status and pod state. A rolling restart briefly halves the egress budget (180 RPS) and produces CPX‑W430 on the sole surviving pod for only a minute or two, while the Deployment reports progress. A missing instance appears as a Pending pod with scheduling events about anti‑affinity or taints, and CPX‑W430 persists longer as the lone pod handles the full traffic. By correlating the duration of CPX‑W430, the rollout status output, and the pod list you can tell which scenario is occurring.","likely_cause":"Insufficient evidence to label a single cause; the observed CPX‑W430 could stem from either a rolling restart or a missing instance and must be resolved by checking rollout and pod status.","confidence":"medium","claims":[{"text":"CPX‑W430 only from one proxy indicates one instance is gone and the survivor handles the whole 180 RPS budget","evidence_ids":["RB-029#4"],"quote":"CPX-W430 only from card-processor-proxy-01... One instance gone; the survivor's 180 is the whole budget"},{"text":"During a rolling restart the Deployment rolls one instance at a time, halving the egress budget to 180 RPS and CPX‑W430 may appear for a minute or two","evidence_ids":["RB-023#3"],"quote":"The Deployment rolls one instance at a time ... egress budget is halved (180 instead of 360 per second). Off-peak, or expect CPX-W430 for the minute or two"},{"text":"A missing proxy instance shows as Pending with scheduling events mentioning anti‑affinity or taints","evidence_ids":["RB-029#4"],"quote":"The missing one is `Pending`, with a scheduling event naming anti-affinity or taints"},{"text":"Rolling restart can be observed via `kubectl rollout restart` followed by `kubectl rollout status` which reports progress without a Pending pod","evidence_ids":["RB-023#3"],"quote":"k rollout restart deploy/card-processor-proxy && k rollout status deploy/card-processor-proxy"},{"text":"Bringing back the missing instance is the usual fastest fix, requiring investigation of node unschedulability","evidence_ids":["RB-029#7"],"quote":"Bring the missing instance back. Usually fastest: find out why its node is unschedulable"}],"next_checks":["Run `kubectl rollout status deploy/card-processor-proxy` to see if a restart is in progress","List proxy pods with `kubectl get pods -l app=card-processor-proxy -o wide` and note any in Pending state","Check timestamps and duration of CPX‑W430 logs; brief (≈1‑2 min) spikes suggest a rollout, prolonged spikes suggest a missing pod","Inspect scheduling events for Pending pods for anti‑affinity or taint reasons","If a pod is Pending, investigate node health and unschedulable conditions before deciding on a manual delete/recreate"]}
